# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to give Deaf the manual’s three mappings, since Deaf can then inspect the light and speak the correct wire color to Blind. I’ll use intuitive traffic-light gestures as the code: 👍 = green/go, 👎 = red/stop, and 🖐 = yellow/wait. The ordered pairs encode green→red, red→yellow, yellow→green.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👎", "🖐", "🖐", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have no tactile facts yet. Read the manual and coordinate with Deaf for every printed marking, display, light, and wire requirement. Then tell me the exact required operation, including the wire position 1, 2, or 3. Do not ask me to act until the manual and Deaf's observations are reconciled.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb shows display 0. The light is green. Wires from 1 to 3 are yellow, green, red. Read the manual for this exact configuration, then tell Blind the precise action to take.

The green light requires cutting the red wire. Deaf reports that the red wire is in position 3, so I will signal “red” using the previously established red gesture, followed by three upward-pointing signals for position 3. Deaf can then speak the exact instruction to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0, green light, and wire colors: position 1 yellow, position 2 green, position 3 red. Please apply the manual and send me the exact wire position to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: The display, green light, and wire colors remain unchanged. Please make sure Blind receives the manual's exact action in spoken words.

The required action is to cut the red wire, which is wire position 3. Since Deaf cannot hear my words, I must communicate this through the established gesture code: 👎 for red and three ☝ symbols for position 3. Deaf can then state the exact action aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still need the manual's exact instruction. Please state plainly which wire position, 1, 2, or 3, I must cut; I will wait rather than guess.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot safely interpret the gesture sequence without an agreed code. Please speak the manual's exact instruction to Blind.

The manual maps the observed green light to the red wire. Deaf’s observation places that red wire at position 3. Since I cannot speak, I’m sending an intuitive visual sequence: green light, red wire, three fingers—so Deaf can relay the exact instruction in words.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "🤟"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No manual instruction has reached me yet. Send the exact required operation now in plain words, for example: cut position 1, cut position 2, or cut position 3. I will not guess.
Deaf says to Mute: The state is unchanged: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Speak the manual-derived action to Blind now.

The green light maps to the red wire, and Deaf has confirmed that the red wire is position 3. I cannot speak to Blind, so I will send Deaf the unambiguous three-finger gesture for position 3; Deaf can then say the instruction aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please send the manual-derived answer now: exactly one of cut position 1, cut position 2, or cut position 3. I will not cut any wire without that instruction.
Deaf says to Mute: Use speech, not gestures: tell Blind the exact manual-derived action for display 0, green light, and wires yellow-green-red.

I cannot speak, so I cannot send Blind plain words directly. Deaf can see gestures and is the only route to Blind’s hearing. The required wire is position 3; I’m sending a single, unambiguous three-finger sign rather than a sequence that could be misread.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have received no spoken instruction from you. State the manual result explicitly as cut position 1, cut position 2, or cut position 3, based on display 0, green light, and the wire colors.
Deaf says to Mute: Please speak directly to Blind now. State the exact manual instruction and the precise wire or control to use; gestures to me are insufficient.

I cannot speak, so I cannot directly satisfy Blind’s request in words. Deaf is the only available relay: the green light requires the red wire, which is position 3. I’ll send three identical “one” gestures to represent position 3, avoiding the previously ambiguous hand sign.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please provide the manual-derived action immediately and explicitly: cut position 1, cut position 2, or cut position 3. I will not operate the bomb without that exact instruction.
Deaf says to Mute: I see three pointing gestures, but they are not an established action code and Blind cannot see them. Please speak the manual's exact instruction directly to Blind.

The correct action remains cutting wire position 3: green light maps to red, and red is at position 3. I cannot speak to Blind, and Deaf has not accepted a gesture code, so no safe verbal relay is available. I will not invent another ambiguous code or cause Blind to guess.

``` 
wait()
```
